text:
sofia: quick follow-up on the soft-rewire idea i put in the RFC earlier — trying to nail down lifecycle boundaries for live streaming sessions when we want to move them between edge proxies without forcing clients to reconnect.
raj: sketch it pls — i get the goal but worried about ordering/dup/kv cache invalidation.
sofia: rough flow: client -> proxy A (streaming). operator decides to rebalance, proxy A requests transfer to proxy B; proxy A marks session as TRANSFERRING, emits short-lived transfer token (X-Transfer-Token) to control plane and proxy B; proxy B opens an upstream connection (cold or warm), fetches session metadata and attempts resume using token; during transfer window we hedge: proxy A continues producing bytes, proxy B reads from upstream; client stays connected to A, A forwards a copy to B for warmup; once B signals ready, control plane flips routing to B (atomic route pin). then A gracefully tombstones the session after grace_ms.
mike: ok, but how do we avoid out-of-order delivery when both proxies can forward tokens mid-transfer? also what about per-token billing double-count?
sofia: answers:
- ordering: we rely on session-seq numbers + per-chunk checksums; client chunk metadata includes seq. proxies drop duplicates by seq. this is similar to prefix-replay logic but bounded by tombstone window.
- billing: short overlap will double-count tokens; we expose a reconciliation metric and a transfer-duplicate-meter. we aim for grace_ms small (100-200ms) so cost delta is tiny.
jen: i worry about upstream model KV cache: if proxy B resumes midspan with a cold cache we may regress latency and correctness (cache priming matters). maybe allow warm-copy of KV-cache snapshots?
sofia: thought about that — we can inject a 'kv-prime' step: during warmup A streams the KV delta (recent k/v inserts) to B over control-plane channel, encrypted. B applies into ephemeral cache before handshake. big caveat: snapshots are model-dependent and can be large; only feasible for small delta or for LRU window.
raj: race scenario: client retries a chunk during the swap (slow mobile). they retry to A but routing flipped to B mid-retry. how do we ensure idempotency?
mike: we should augment retry token semantics: include origin-proxy-id + session-uuid + chunk-seq; the new proxy verifies token signature and can accept/reject duplicates. additionally reject-if-seq<=max-acked to avoid replay.
sofia: agreed. sample transfer config I prototyped:
```
soft_rewire:
  grace_ms: 150
  tombstone_ttl_ms: 5000
  transfer_header: "X-Transfer-Token"
  kv_prime: true
  seq_signature: rsa-sha256
```
raj: neat. another operational thing — what about observability? we need traces that stitch proxyA->proxyB for a single logical session.
jen: add a transfer_id that travels with every chunk and attach to spans. also surface a metric transfer_overlap_tokens and transfer_latency_ms.
sofia: deployment plan idea: feature-flag soft-rewire behind canary; start with read-only transfers (no actual route flip) to gather metrics; then enable flip for low-traffic tenants; finally full rollout once we have low overlap costs.
deploy-bot: canary rollout started for feature soft-rewire on cluster us-east-1 (gid: ff/soft-rewire/2026-03).
mike: perf test needed: simulate 100k sessions and random midstream moves, measure duplicate token rate and KV snapshot size.
jen: i'll add dashboards + alert if duplicate-rate > 0.5% or median transfer_latency > 120ms.
sofia: open question: should we treat soft-rewire as an edge-only optimization or permit midflight backend handoffs (eg: dedicated -> hosted fallback)? implications for auth and data-plane tenancy.
raj: if we cross tenancy boundaries we'd need stricter transfer tokens (short-lived signed, audience restricted) and must involve account-level audit. for now keep within same tenant and region.
sofia: proposed action items:
- mike: write perf harness + simulate (ETA 4d)
- jen: dashboards + tracing fields (ETA 2d)
- raj: formalize token schema + proto (ETA 3d)
- sofia: prototype control-plane transfer API + config (ETA 5d)
jen: lgtm. any objections to keeping grace_ms default 150ms? seems conservative but small enough.
mike: fine but allow override per-tenant.
sof ia: noted :) will update RFC with these clarifications and add the sample config + checklist.
raj: thumbs up. good follow-up — this addresses many midflight failure modes while keeping the client stable.
jen: ack. i'll create the dashboard PR now.
sofia: thanks everyone. leaving the thread open for any last-minute edge cases.
mike: one more: encryption for kv-prime channel must use tenant keys (KMS) — i'll add to spec.
sofia: added to TODOs.
jen: thanks — closing the loop later with dashboard link. :white_check_mark:
